summary: Decision (owner fdev, FS-GG/FS.GG.Game#727): the profile policy deadline (250 ms) bounds guest policy work only. A load still creates the module Worker and posts its command at once; the Worker's first Compile receipt for that command is its readiness report. Before readiness the control is projected in phase 'start' under a separate startup bound (HostSettings default 5000 ms, selectable 1-60000 ms, capped by any caller enclosing deadline, so receivers wanting only the policy budget pass none for loads); expiry there is the distinct appended DeliveryReason.WorkerStartTimeout (Discarded, TimedOut/Compile, not dispatched, Worker terminated, no game authority). Readiness replaces the startup timer with the policy timer. Compilation, phase and digest receipts before readiness, repeated readiness and readiness after expiry are inert; Worker failure, termination or a protocol-violating invocation receipt before readiness still faults the starting Worker. Ready-Worker requests keep enqueue budgets. The canonical lifecycle model, schedules (default 58/selected 16), F# correspondence and unit tests agree; coherent source version 0.7.0, ApiCompat-compatible with published 0.6.0. Lesson: Firefox reduced timer precision lets setTimeout callbacks observe floor(performance.now()) <= due (measured 36/300; Chromium/WebKit 0/300). A connected-interpreter timer observation that expires nothing was never re-armed, so a looping guest could hang unretired (intermittent 15 s Firefox watchdog hangs); the interpreter now delivers timer observations only after the clock passes due and re-arms the remainder. Lesson: WebKit words wasm traps 'Unreachable code ...'; compare trap diagnostics case-insensitively. Sampling: requiring an explicit readiness step made the selected frozen-commit-expiry witness (a 1-in-1000 lucky sample on main, 0 at four other seeds) unreachable; an initialized-candidate sampled entry makes it structurally reachable (14/1000) instead of changing the pinned seed. Evidence at capture: hosted wasm-shared run 39881900333 on PR728 head 1f68f96 (4 vCPU, 20 fresh-profile cold loads per browser, artifact wasm-cold-load-39881900333-1) measured startup max Chromium 37 ms, Firefox 76 ms, WebKit 52 ms and policy-load max 5.7/8/9 ms; the same suite passed in all three browsers. These are finite samples on the bundled 0.7 Worker, not a future fit guarantee. Publication, Templates re-pin and installed acceptance are separate later boundaries.
title: Worker startup is bounded separately from the WASM policy deadline; Firefox timers can fire before due
